name: Kitunusi
body:
KITUNUSI
CR 4

This striking, muscular figure with sharply pointed ears is clad in a bright blue cape. An unplaceable strangeness lingers in their presence.

XP 1,200
LN Medium fey
Init +3; Senses low-light vision; Perception +11
Aura frightful presence (30 ft., DC 15, frightened for 1d4 rounds)

DEFENSE

AC 17, touch 14, flat-footed 14 (+3 Dex, +1 luck, +3 natural)
hp 39 (6d6+18)
Fort +6, Ref +9, Will +8
Defensive Abilities hitching dance; DR 5/cold iron

OFFENSE

Speed 30 ft.
Melee unarmed strike +8 (1d8+5)
Special Attacks death touch

STATISTICS

Str 20, Dex 16, Con 17, Int 12, Wis 15, Cha 15
Base Atk +3; CMB +8 (+12 grapple); CMD 21 (23 vs. grapple)
Feats Greater Grapple, Improved Grapple, Improved Unarmed Strike
Skills Acrobatics +12, Climb +14, Diplomacy +11, Knowledge (nature) +10, Perception +11, Sense Motive +11, Survival +8
Languages Common, Elven, Sylvan
SQ accomplished wrestler

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Accomplished Wrestler (Ex)

A kitunusi deals unarmed strike damage as a monk of the same level as its Hit Dice. It can deal lethal or nonlethal damage with its unarmed strikes and while grappling. A kitunusi uses its Hit Dice in place of base attack bonus for the purpose of qualifying for feats which have Improved Grapple as a prerequisite.

Death Touch (Su)

As a standard action, a kitunusi touches a creature within reach (+8 melee touch). On a hit, the creature takes 4d8+5 points of negative energy damage and has a –4 penalty on checks to stabilize when dying. This penalty also applies to checks made by others to stabilize the affected creature (such as providing first aid using the Heal skill). A successful DC 15 Will save halves the damage and negates the stabilization check penalty. Remove curse or restoration can remove this penalty. This is a curse effect. The save DC is Wisdom-based.

Hitching Dance (Su)

As a swift action, a kitunusi hitches itself into a seated posture, walking on its hands instead of its feet. While in this position, the kitunusi gains a +30-foot enhancement bonus to its land speed, isn’t hindered by difficult terrain, and doesn’t provoke attacks of opportunity when leaving threatened squares.

A kitunusi can activate its frightful presence when using hitching dance.

Kitunusi Garment (Su)

Each kitunusi wears a blue garment—a cape, scarf, shawl, or other item of clothing—at all times. This garment grants the kitunusi a +1 luck bonus on saving throws and to AC (included in the statistics above). The garment is an extension of the kitunusi, it isn’t possible to steal the garment in its entirety; it is a physical extension of the kitunusi.

The kitunusi can gift a thread of its garment to a creature it favors. Each day the gifted creature retains the thread, it multiplies subtly, becoming a garment of the same type worn by the kitunusi after a month. This gifted garment gives +1 luck bonus on saving throws and to Armor Class, and takes up the body magic item slot. It doesn’t function until it is finished growing and regenerates if damaged, but any pieces separated from it become worthless string.

Fey creatures instinctively recognize this created garment as being fairly gifted to its wearer. The wearer gains a +2 circumstance bonus on Diplomacy checks when interacting with fey creatures and most fey have a starting attitude one step more favorable than usual toward the wearer.

A kitunusi remains aware of all creatures that possess a thread or garment grown from its own garment, and their locations. If a creature attempts to sell or give away the garment it was gifted, or if another creature steals the garment, the kitunusi knows what has happened. The kitunusi can decide to curse the originally gifted creature (see below), to allow the new creature to keep the gifted garment, to curse the new creature, or have the gifted garment to crumble to dust. At any time, the kitunusi can choose to withdraw its favor, causing the thread or garment to turn to dust.

A creature who steals a thread from a kitunusi has a very different experience. The garment grows and acts like a gifted garment, except that it is cursed. The garment changes from providing bonuses to giving a –1 penalty on saving throws and to AC, and its color changes to yellow. All fey have a starting attitude of hostile toward the wearer and their attitudes cannot be improved in the wearer’s presence. Fey creatures also gain a +4 circumstance bonus to Sense Motive checks made against the wearer. The cursed garment can only be removed via remove curse or similar magic. Breaking the curse severs the connection with the kitunusi, causing the garment to dissolve into dust.

ECOLOGY

Environment warm forests
Organization solitary
Treasure kitunusi garment

Kitunusi are affable fey who live for the joy of wrestling and the sanctity of hospitality. They are the truest of friends to those who show respectful courtesy and are entertaining guests, but can be implacable foes to any who offend or steal from them. Though they resemble humans or elves in stature and general form, an unidentifiable otherness marks them as something else.

Kitunusi are bound by ancient laws of hospitality, and unlike some fey, they believe in honoring both their letter and their spirit. Those they grant protection or shelter are fiercely defended, even unto death. Kitunusi only withdraw their hospitality when such trust is abused. A guest who proves especially entertaining, or one to whom a kitunusi feels indebted, may be honored with a thread from its garment, offered as a token of gratitude.

Kitunusi delight in physical contests and are overjoyed when challenged to a wrestling match, or when a creature accepts their invitation to one. The kitunusi and its opponent engage in a series of grappling bouts, each striving to pin the other. The first to win three bouts is declared the victor. If the challenger prevails, the kitunusi offers a thread from its own garment as a mark of favor. Regardless of the outcome, the challenger and any compatriots are warmly invited to rest beside the kitunusi’s campfire.

Variant

Aquatic kitunusi are less common than their land-bound cousins, though hardly rare. Their statistics are the same, except they have the aquatic subtype, the amphibious special quality, a 30-foot swim speed, and Swim +22 instead of Climb.
